meta.title: Community
meta.description: Who we are and how we behave. A no-toxicity gaming community with weekly events, mentorship for newcomers, and voice channels that are always busy.

header.title: Built in a Voice Channel, Still Feels Like One
header.lead: Beyond the games: reliable teammates, new friends, and lasting connections with people who understand the grind without needing it explained.

who.title: A Global Community With a Small-Server Feel
paragraphs: Gamer's Exile started in a five-person voice channel and never lost the feeling of one. We are a diverse, global community bringing together casual players, hardcore competitors, content creators, and everyone in the wide space between.

Whether you are grinding ranked matches, building a streaming career, or just looking for people to squad up with on a Tuesday night, this was built for you. We believe gaming is best when it is shared — and our members prove that every single day.

values.title: Four Things We Do Not Compromise On
values.lead: Every community says it is welcoming. These are the specific behaviours we actually enforce.

respect.title: Respect First
respect.body: Trash talk stays in the match. Everyone here is someone's teammate, and we treat them that way — in voice, in chat, and after a loss.

noToxicity.title: A No-Toxicity Zone
noToxicity.body: Harassment, slurs and deliberate tilting get you removed. Not warned repeatedly, not debated in modmail. Removed. The bar is the whole point.

mentors.title: Veterans Mentor Newcomers
mentors.body: Nobody gets gatekept for being new. Our veterans run coaching nights, VOD reviews and starter squads because someone once did it for them.

celebrate.title: Every Grind Is Celebrated
celebrate.body: First win or first tournament title, Bronze to Radiant or a hundred-viewer milestone — it gets posted, and people cheer. Win or lose.

rhythm.title: There Is Always Something On
rhythm.lead: Regular fixtures through the week, plus whatever spontaneously happens in voice at 2am. All times UTC.
rhythm.leadEmpty: The weekly schedule is being planned. Activities and events are announced in the Discord first, then listed here.
rhythm.emptyBody: Join the {discord} to hear first when activities are announced.

voice.title: The Voice Channels Never Really Empty
voice.body: Our voice channels are always buzzing. There is nearly always someone looking to team up, talk strategy, or just decompress after a long match — whatever hour you keep.

items.q: Do I need to be good at games to join?
items.a: No. We have Radiant players and people who installed their first shooter last week, and both get a squad. Skill decides which tournament bracket you enter, not whether you belong here.
Nothing. Membership is free and always will be. There are no paid roles, no pay-to-enter tournaments, and no perks locked behind a subscription.

items.q: Which games do you actually play?
items.a: Everything. The tournament slate rotates through the big competitive titles, but the server has channels for RPGs, MMOs, fighters, racing sims and indie games. If you bring a game nobody plays yet, you will usually find three people willing to try it.

items.q: I'm a streamer. What do I get out of this?
items.a: Go-live pings that people respond to, a weekly raid train slot, clip and shoutout support across our channels, and honest feedback on your setup. We do not require exclusivity and we do not take a cut of anything.

items.q: How do I enter a tournament?
items.a: Join the Discord, take the tournament role, and sign up in the registration channel before the bracket locks. Solo players can request a team in the same channel — we place a lot of squads that way.

items.q: What happens if someone is toxic?
items.a: Report it to a mod with a screenshot or a clip. Harassment and slurs are a removal, not a warning cycle. Our moderators are active in voice, not just in text, which is where most of it actually happens.
